title: Migration header still says continue_token is 'minted lazily' and 'most rows have NULL' — contradicted by round-2 W1 mint-at-save
evidence:
-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).
detail: Round-2 W1 changed upsert_application_draft.sql to mint the token at SAVE time (its header: 'The continue token is minted at SAVE time (COALESCE keeps an existing one)'). Most rows will now carry a token, so this migration comment is stale; merged migrations are immutable per AGENTS.md.
recommended_fix: Update the header comment before merge to state the token is minted at first save (COALESCE-preserved) so every live draft is reachable by the stage-2 continue-link.

title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row' — contradicted by round-2 W3 tombstone design documented in the same file
evidence:
--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
detail: Round-2 W3 made erasure a tombstone: erase_draft_by_token.sql wipes fields/token and sets erased_at, keeping the (vacancy, email) suppression key — exactly what this file's own erased_at column comment describes. The header line contradicts both; fix pre-merge since migrations can't be edited once merged.
recommended_fix: Reword the header bullet to 'tombstones the row (fields/token wiped, erased_at set; key kept as suppression record until vacancy close)'.
